trickyParts: The notice sits at the two call sites that newly enter the wait (merged, and transition's already-merged branch) and nowhere else. Notices never de-duplicate — effects.go's notice writes a row per call — and closeMerged is re-entered on every child's departure (closeAwaitingRoot) and on every daemon boot (sweepMerged), so a notice inside the rule would send one per departure and one per restart for as long as the root waits, which may be days. closeMergedTelling is the one body those two share.

Rule 1 reads the parent relation downward and Rule 2 reads the flat tree, and they must not be merged. Every member of a tree names the root in its tree field, so an acceptance held for any member of its tree would wait for the root, which is waiting for it; the close reads the flat tree because the linger stops every member whatever it hangs under.

The wait is kept inside closeMerged's branch where the tree does not linger. A member of a tree that already lingers must still close at its merge — TestALingeringMembersMergeClosesItAndWakesItsCheck holds that — and a merge is the one fact GitHub never sends again.

openBeneath's three termination rules are the daemon's own upward walk's (api/architect.go, owns): a visited set, because issues.parent is plain nullable text with no foreign key rewritten from every Dispatch observation, so a cycle would spin inside the fact's database transaction; only issues the tree lists are followed; an issue whose parent is empty or names a key the tree does not hold is beneath nothing.

The contract bump had to land with the field: the boot gate refuses a daemon whose number differs from the installed plugin's, which I met head-on while booting the shipped binary for the state readback.

The two live proof scripts are read and edited, never run: stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh runs for hours on an operator's machine against the production cluster, Dispatch and Envoy with credentials no issue pod holds, and stage3-devbox-workflow.sh needs a devbox. stage4b's two removed checkpoints had dependants in eight further places in the script, two of its library tests, its README and AGENTS.md, each followed through; the `close` checkpoint's tree_gone now also names the two children the run parks, which the removal would otherwise have left unasserted.

The spec asks for the proof on a daemon booted by the shipped legion start. That binary cannot host either rule in a pod: with no dispatch_url openWorkflow returns nothing and the daemon registers no handlers, and with dispatch_url set boot mints an installation token per owner from both GitHub Apps' private keys, which no worker pod holds. The proof therefore boots run, the function legion start calls, through the daemon package's whole-daemon harness with the e2e build tag — the repository's established shape, controller_sweep_live_test.go with scripts/e2e/controller-sweep-kind.sh — and the shipped binary appears in the hand-run /healthz and legion state --json readback above. The architect accepted this shape and asked for both of those quoted on the pull request, which they are.

The spec says the implementer gets its database as a workload in the cluster. That route is closed on this pod: docs/kubernetes.md's gate says to submit nothing unless all three commands answer a bare yes, and kubectl auth can-i create services and get services both answer no here. The database is the zonky embedded PostgreSQL the repository has recorded twice (LEGION-668, LEGION-694), and the proof script hard-requires LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN and starts none itself, so CI's service, a devbox container and the pod's jar all satisfy it and the tester can re-run it anywhere. No blocker: everything the boot needs runs where the work happens.
discoveredComplexity: Task 7's audit found no hole: every way a member stops holding its root runs leave. A status moving to backlog, icebox, triage or done goes through dispatchIssue's OutOfWorkflow branch; a phase reaching done goes through transition's row.To == phase.Done; close_root and LeaveUnslotted call it directly. phase.Done is written nowhere else but inside leave, beginLinger and leaveUnderOperator, and the last two end the root rather than a member. The one path that changes an issue's tree without leave — a handed-over child re-admitted as a root of its own — cannot reach a waiting root: orphan requires !record.TreeLive, and a waiting root holds its admission slot (releaseDoneSlots frees only at phase done, releaseInactiveSlots only at phase done or an out-of-workflow status, and a waiting root is awaiting_merge at status retro) and does not linger. The boot's sweep is the backstop. leave's doc comment now states this.
